summary: Sh. Ali Mashhour discusses a hadith from Sahih Muslim about the nature of sin and repentance in Islam. The hadith states that if believers did not commit sins and seek forgiveness, Allah would replace them with people who would sin and repent. Sh. Ali Mashhour explains the Islamic understanding of different types of sins: ism (matters of the heart), them (sins between a person and Allah), and say (sins involving others' rights). He emphasizes that repentance is central to human purpose and that making mistakes followed by genuine repentance is part of a well-rounded human existence, distinguishing human imperfection from divine perfection.
suggested_title: The Purpose of Repentance: Understanding Sin and Forgiveness in Islam
catchy_title: Why Allah Wants You to Repent
